paragraphs: A Brahmin was setting off to visit a disciple's house and needed a porter to carry his luggage. He could not find anyone from what he considered a respectable caste, so at last he asked a shoemaker.

The shoemaker said no at first. He belonged to an untouchable caste, he explained, and it would not be proper. But the Brahmin insisted. Just stay completely silent, he told him, and no one will ever find out.

Eventually the man agreed. When they reached the disciple's house, someone told the new servant to take off a pair of shoes. Remembering his instructions to keep quiet, the servant did not respond. The order was repeated, and still nothing. Finally the person lost patience and shouted at him: was he deaf? Was he a shoemaker or something?
The poor man panicked. He cried out to the Brahmin, "O Master, I am discovered." He could not stay a moment longer, and with that he ran off as fast as his legs would carry him.
learn: The story pokes fun at how silly caste prejudice is: the whole elaborate cover-up collapses at the first ordinary request. Systems built on hiding who people are will always fall apart. Better to treat everyone with dignity from the start.
